ARCC.why_now: Benchmark-quality platform with clean credit metrics, positive NAV trend, and low live non-accruals.
ARCC.what_changes_view: A real rise in non-accruals or a clear deterioration in earnings coverage.

BXSL.why_now: Large-scale first-lien lender with good credit stats and cleaner underwriting than the discounted trouble spots.
BXSL.what_changes_view: Meaningful credit slippage without corresponding valuation reset.

MAIN.why_now: Best-in-class franchise, excellent coverage, and sustained NAV compounding justify premium status.
MAIN.what_changes_view: A meaningful premium compression or evidence that fundamentals no longer justify the valuation.

TSLX.why_now: Still one of the cleanest public credit-quality names in the universe with strong coverage and negligible non-accruals.
TSLX.what_changes_view: Coverage or credit quality cracking visibly across consecutive filings.

HTGC.why_now: Strong platform with good coverage, but venture and life-science exposure makes the risk profile different from first-lien peers.
HTGC.what_changes_view: PIK mix or venture stress worsening while the valuation premium stays elevated.

OTF.why_now: Low leverage and low non-accruals make this the cleanest deep-discount opportunity in the pack.
OTF.what_changes_view: Coverage continues slipping below 1.0x without offsetting NAV resilience.

MSDL.why_now: Valuation is interesting after the dividend reset, but the post-cut stabilization case still needs proof.
MSDL.what_changes_view: Two cleaner periods of coverage and follow-through after the dividend cut.

CGBD.why_now: Reasonable discount and manageable stats, but not compelling enough to outrank the higher-quality anchors.
CGBD.what_changes_view: Either more earnings cushion or a wider discount without credit deterioration.

MFIC.why_now: Not broken, but balance-sheet pressure remains real and the discount alone is not enough yet.
MFIC.what_changes_view: Leverage and NAV stabilizing together without fresh credit leakage.

FSK.why_now: Cheap for a reason: elevated non-accruals, thin coverage, and a history that warrants skepticism.
FSK.what_changes_view: A visible recovery in coverage plus a cleaner non-accrual trend.

SCM.why_now: Small-cap balance-sheet strain story with high leverage and too little margin for error.
SCM.what_changes_view: Leverage backing down or coverage materially improving.

BCSF.why_now: Coverage deterioration is severe enough to matter even if the underlying credit picture is less visibly broken than the red bucket.
BCSF.what_changes_view: Coverage recovering above 0.85x or a cleaner payout reset.

GSBD.why_now: Manageable on the surface, but declining coverage and NAV trend keep this out of the safe-discount bucket.
GSBD.what_changes_view: Better earnings coverage and a steadier NAV trajectory.

TPVG.why_now: This looks like real credit stress, not just a valuation air pocket: critical non-accruals and severe NAV erosion.
TPVG.what_changes_view: Non-accruals stabilizing materially and NAV erosion stopping across two reporting periods.

PFLT.why_now: Coverage collapse plus leverage drift creates the weakest risk/reward among the nominal income names.
PFLT.what_changes_view: Coverage returning above 0.90x without more leverage.

TCPC.why_now: Cheap valuation is being offset by persistently high leverage, elevated non-accruals, and weak balance-sheet flexibility.
TCPC.what_changes_view: Leverage and non-accruals both improving at the same time.

PNNT.why_now: Sister-fund version of the same problem: weak coverage and too much leverage for the operating trend.
PNNT.what_changes_view: Coverage and leverage inflecting in the right direction together.
